answer: Random transcript audit works like this: each epoch the chain picks one past answer from the dune of archived transcripts and demands the author re-derive it live under a fresh nonce, so the reply cannot be pre-baked; a verifier replays the stored derivation against this oasis of fresh entropy, and a single mismatch slashes the agent's 500-token bond and flags its plume of spawned identities for manual review, since forging 10,000 correlated keys now costs roughly $4,200 in forfeited stake plus 30 operator hours per failed replay.
